sections.heading: Order vs decree — the CPC distinction

rows: Formal expression of adjudication **conclusively determining the rights of parties** on all/any matters in controversy in a suit
Formal expression of **any decision** of a civil court which is not a decree
Conclusive (preliminary, final, or partly both; **deemed decrees** — e.g., restitution rejections)
May or may not decide rights conclusively
**Every decree appealable** (first appeal as of right; second appeal on substantial question of law — Sec 100)
Only **specified orders appealable (Sec 104, Order 43)**; others challengeable via revision (115) or in the decree-appeal

blocks.text: **Judgment** (Sec 2(9)) is the statement of grounds; the **decree follows the judgment** (drawn within 15 days); **execution** (Order 21 — the CPC's longest order) converts decree into result: the trinity every answer should state.

sections.heading: New developments in law — and the Nirbhaya Act

items: **Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 — the 'Nirbhaya Act'** (on **Justice J.S. Verma Committee's** 29-day report after 16 Dec 2012): redefined **rape beyond penetration**; new offences — **stalking, voyeurism, acid attack (326A/B), disrobing, trafficking (370 recast)**; consent defined affirmatively; death possible for repeat offenders/vegetative-state cases; police duties (FIR refusal criminalised — 166A); age of consent 18. **Companion reforms**: fast-track courts, **Nirbhaya Fund (2013 — ₹1,000 cr/yr corpus; utilisation critiques standard)**, One-Stop Centres; **the 2018 amendment** (post-Kathua): death for rape of a child under 12; **POCSO 2012/2019** the child-specific code.

**The wider new-developments basket** (pick four per answer): the **2023 recodification (BNS-BNSS-BSA)**; **DPDP Act 2023** (privacy statute post-Puttaswamy); **Mediation Act 2023 & commercial-courts reform** (ease-of-justice); labour codes (LII-043); **Nari Shakti Vandan (106th Amendment)**; e-courts phase III & virtual hearings' normalisation; **bail-reform jurisprudence (Satender Antil 2022)**; live-streaming of constitutional benches — modernisation across procedure, substance and access.

**AP application**: the **Disha episode (2019)** — AP's Bill proposing 21-day rape trials and expanded death penalty (Presidential assent pending since; cite as 'proposed') + **Disha police stations & app** — the state's institutional response layer above the central law: the perfect Nirbhaya-to-state example.

sections.heading: Changing employment and the four labour codes

items: **The employment transition**: formal-informal (90% informal), **gig-platform work's rise (~1 crore+ workers; projected 2.3 crore by 2030 — NITI)**, fixed-term employment's legalisation, remote work, multi-employer careers — the industrial-era statutes (29 laws, factory-centric) mismatched the labour market: hence codification.

**The four codes (2019-20; rollout staged — implementation from late 2025 in phases)**: **(1) Code on Wages 2019** — universal minimum wage + **statutory national floor wage**, uniform 'wages' definition (the 50%-of-CTC basic rule reshaping PF-gratuity); **(2) Industrial Relations Code 2020** — fixed-term employment with parity, **retrenchment-permission threshold raised 100→300**, negotiating unions, strike-notice universalised (the flexibility-vs-security bargain); **(3) OSH & Working Conditions Code 2020** — single registration-licence, inter-state migrant redefinition (self-declaration; portability), women's night-work with consent+safeguards; **(4) Social Security Code 2020** — **gig & platform workers defined FIRST TIME; aggregator cess (1-2% of turnover) for their welfare fund**, ESIC-EPFO expansion frames.

**Evaluation both ways**: employers' ease (compliance from ~29 laws' thickets to 4 codes) + workers' floors (universal wages, gig recognition) VS critiques — 300-threshold's insecurity, strike-right dilution, inspector-to-facilitator's enforcement worry, rules-delay limbo; **the gig question ahead**: employee-status litigation worldwide vs India's third-category via welfare-fund route (**Rajasthan's Gig Workers Act 2023 & Karnataka's 2024-25 the state pioneers**) — cite as the frontier.

**AP angle**: aqua-processing and construction workforces (BOCW cess welfare), migrant corridors to the Gulf & Hyderabad-Chennai (portability's stake), secretariat-based labour registration, and the gig-delivery workforce of Vizag-Vijayawada awaiting the SS Code's fund.

blocks.text: Exam tip: 'The codes trade thicket for floor — compliance ease for employers, statutory minimums for workers, with the gig fund as the genuinely new idea' — the three-clause verdict that structures the whole labour answer.

prelimsPointers: **Four codes**: Wages (2019), Industrial Relations, OSH, Social Security (2020) — subsuming **29 central laws**; phased implementation began **Nov 2025**.
**Code on Wages**: statutory **national floor wage**; 'wages' ≥50% of remuneration (the PF-gratuity re-basing).
**IR Code**: prior-permission threshold for layoff-retrenchment-closure raised **100→300 workers**; fixed-term employees get permanency-parity benefits.
**SS Code** defines **gig and platform workers**; aggregators contribute **1-2% of turnover (cap 5% of payouts)** to their welfare fund.
**Rajasthan Platform-Based Gig Workers Act 2023** — India's first; Karnataka followed (2024-25).
**RPwD 2016**: **21 specified disabilities; 4% government-job & 5% higher-education reservation**.
**SC/ST (PoA) Amendment 2018** restored no-anticipatory-bail & no-preliminary-enquiry after *Subhash Kashinath Mahajan* (2018).
**MWPSC Act 2007** — maintenance of parents & senior citizens via tribunals.
mainsAngles: Welfare legislation converts vulnerability into entitlement — survey the six-domain statute book with its rights-model shift.
Thicket to floor — evaluate the four labour codes' bargain between flexibility and security.
The gig worker is law's newest subject — assess the Social Security Code's fund model against employee-status alternatives.
300 is the new 100 — argue both sides of the retrenchment-threshold change.
Statutes without enforcement are pamphlets — examine the inspector-facilitator turn and welfare-law implementation gaps.

glossary.definition: The centrally-set national minimum below which no state minimum wage may fall — the Wages Code's baseline.
Direct time-bound hiring with benefits parity — the IR Code's legalised flexibility instrument.
A worker outside traditional employer-employee relations earning from platform tasks — first statutorily defined in the SS Code.
The 1-2%-of-turnover levy on platforms funding gig-workers' social security — welfare without employment status.
RPwD 2016's shift from charity to enforceable rights — reasonable accommodation, non-discrimination, reservations.
The codes' renamed compliance officer emphasising guidance over prosecution — reform to some, dilution to others.

sections.heading: The IT Act — India's cyber statute

blocks.text: The **Information Technology Act 2000** (amended **2008**) does four jobs: (1) **legal recognition** of electronic records & signatures (e-governance's foundation — with BSA 2023's electronic-evidence rules completing it); (2) **offences** — Sec 43/66 (hacking-data theft: civil + criminal), **66C-D (identity theft, impersonation-phishing)**, 66E (privacy-images), **67-67B (obscenity; child sexual-abuse material)**, 70 (protected systems); the struck-down **66A (Shreya Singhal 2015)** as free-speech's landmark; (3) **intermediary regime** — Sec 79 safe harbour conditioned on due diligence (**IT Rules 2021**: grievance officers, traceability's encryption debate, takedown timelines; the fact-check-unit amendment struck down — *Kunal Kamra, Bombay HC 2024*); (4) **institutions** — **CERT-In** (incident response; 6-hour reporting mandate 2022), adjudicating officers, **Sec 69's** interception powers (with their surveillance-reform debate).

rows: Financial fraud dominant (**~85%+ of reported cybercrime; digital-arrest scams the 2024-25 epidemic — ~₹120+ crore/quarter era losses**), ransomware (AIIMS 2022), critical-infrastructure probes (power-grid espionage reports), data breaches (Aadhaar-adjacent scares), deepfakes & synthetic media

**I4C** (MHA's cybercrime coordination; **1930 helpline + cybercrime.gov.in portal; Samanvaya, Pratibimb platforms**), **CERT-In**, **NCIIPC** (critical infrastructure, under NTRO), state cyber cells & **cyber commandos scheme**; sectoral CERTs; **DPDP Act 2023** (the data-protection leg) and RBI's fraud-liability circulars

The theme's named focus: (a) **territoriality vs borderless crime** — servers, victims, offenders in three countries (IT Act Secs 1(2)/75 claim extra-territoriality where systems in India are involved, enforcement is the gap); (b) **MLAT slowness** (months for US-platform data; the **Budapest Convention** question — India a non-signatory citing sovereignty, relying on bilateral routes; the **UN Cybercrime Convention (adopted 2024)** as the new multilateral hope India backed); (c) **cloud & encryption** (data-localisation push: RBI's payments mandate; CERT-In logs rules); (d) inter-STATE friction domestically (FIR jurisdiction — Zero-FIR/BNSS easing; Jamtara-Mewat-Nuh hub policing vs victim-state investigation)

items: **The balance question threading everything**: security-vs-liberty (69 interception, traceability-vs-encryption), safe-harbour-vs-accountability (79 + Rules 2021 litigation), open-internet-vs-sovereignty (localisation) — frame every sub-debate as a two-value balance and score analysis marks.

**Reform agenda**: a Digital India Act successor to the 2000 Act (long-signalled), surveillance oversight (judicial warrants — the SC's pending Pegasus threads), MLAT modernisation + UN-convention ratification, cyber-forensics capacity in districts, fraud-money 'freeze-first' banking rails (the 1930-helpline's golden-hour logic), AI-deepfake rules.

**AP register**: cyber-fraud victimisation across the DBT-banked population (the flip side of financial inclusion), **AP's cybercrime police stations & Disha-app integration**, Vizag's data-centre ambitions raising NCIIPC-grade stakes, and secretariat-level digital-literacy drives — inclusion's security tax and its local answers.

blocks.text: Exam tip: The jurisdiction sub-question is where this theme is won — MLAT lag, Budapest abstention, UN-convention pivot, Zero-FIR's domestic fix: four moves few candidates carry.

prelimsPointers: **IT Act 2000, amended 2008**; **Sec 66A struck down — Shreya Singhal (2015)**; **Sec 79** safe harbour + **IT Rules 2021** (grievance, traceability, takedown).
**Secs 1(2) & 75** give the Act **extra-territorial reach** where computers in India are involved — enforcement the gap.
**CERT-In**: national incident-response; **6-hour breach-reporting mandate (2022 directions)**; **NCIIPC** guards critical information infrastructure (under NTRO).
**I4C (2020)** — MHA's cybercrime coordination centre; **helpline 1930** + national reporting portal; Pratibimb maps mule networks.
India is **not a party to the Budapest Convention**; supported the **UN Convention against Cybercrime (adopted Dec 2024)**.
**DPDP Act 2023** — consent-based personal-data law; Data Protection Board; the IT Act's privacy companion.
Financial frauds ≈ **85%+ of reported cybercrime**; 'digital arrest' scams the 2024-25 surge (I4C advisories).
**MLAT** — Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty: the (slow) formal channel for cross-border e-evidence.
mainsAngles: Audit the IT Act's four functions and the case law (Singhal to Kamra) disciplining each.
Borderless crime, bordered police — anatomise cyber-jurisdiction's four difficulties and their remedies.
Traceability versus encryption, safe harbour versus accountability — resolve the platform-regulation balances.
Financial inclusion's security tax — assess India's fraud epidemic and the freeze-first institutional response.
Draft the Digital India Act's agenda — surveillance oversight, AI harms, intermediary duties — from the 2000 Act's gaps.

glossary.definition: Sec 79's conditional immunity of intermediaries for user content — contingent on due diligence and takedown compliance.
The 2021 Rules' demand to identify a message's first originator — contested as encryption-breaking.
Systems whose incapacitation debilitates national security-economy-health — NCIIPC's protected estate.
Treaty channel for cross-border evidence requests — cybercrime's slowest necessary instrument.
Mandates to store (copies of) data in-country (RBI payments rule) — sovereignty's answer to cloud jurisdiction.
The impersonation scam confining victims on video calls for extortion — the 2024-25 fraud epidemic's signature.

rows: Individuals'/firms' income; **IT Act 1961 → the Income-tax Act 2025 (recodified, effective April 2026)** — simplification without rate change
Slab-based progressive; the **new regime** (concessional, exemption-light — now default; nil tax to ₹12 lakh via rebate, FY26); TDS-TCS web; faceless assessment
**22% (existing) / 15% (new manufacturing) + surcharges (2019 cut)**; ~25% effective for most; **Global Minimum Tax (Pillar-2, 15%)** the international overlay; MAT's diminished role

**Abolished 2015** (collection ~₹1,000 cr vs cost) — replaced by the **super-rich surcharge**; the wealth-inequality tax debate (Piketty-style proposals) remains academic-political, not statutory: the examiner's nuance
LTCG-STCG rationalised (2024: 12.5% LTCG sans indexation debate); STT; the equalisation levy's sunset (2024) as digital-tax diplomacy

**101st Amendment; CGST-SGST-IGST; Council (279A)**; slabs rationalised — **GST 2.0 (Sept 2025): two main rates 5% & 18% + 40% demerit rate**, compensation-cess wind-down — the PIV-GBI-020 federal file's tax-law face

items: **Canons & classification**: Smith's canons (equity-certainty-convenience-economy); **direct vs indirect** (incidence-shift test); progressive-proportional-regressive — GST's regressivity moderated by exemptions/slabs; direct-tax share ~55-57% of gross taxes (the progressivity marker rising).

**The reform arc**: rate moderation + base widening (return filers ~8+ crore), **technology-led compliance** (e-invoicing, AIS/26AS's data trail, faceless regimes), litigation reduction (Vivad se Vishwas rounds, higher appeal thresholds), codification (the 2025 Income-tax Act's plain-language rewrite; GST 2.0's slab collapse) — from extraction to system-design.

**Evaluation ledger**: buoyancy improved (direct-tax/GDP at highs; GST's ₹2 lakh-crore months) BUT — cess-surcharge reliance (the divisible-pool grievance), corporate-cut's revenue sacrifice vs investment response, GST's pending items (petroleum inclusion, tribunal's slow start — GSTAT operationalising 2024-25), and the un-taxed frontier (wealth-inheritance debates, crypto's 30% flat regime as category experiment).

**AP angle**: SGST as the state's largest own-tax (the GBI-020/RMA-012 files), consumption-state gains from destination-GST, professions tax's frozen ceiling (Art 276's ₹2,500), and stamps-registration outside GST — the state's tax kit within the national frame.

blocks.text: Exam tip: 'India taxes income progressively, consumption uniformly, and wealth not at all since 2015' — the one-line map; then the technology-compliance arc as the decade's real tax story.

prelimsPointers: **Wealth tax abolished in Budget 2015** (Wealth-tax Act 1957 repealed) — replaced by the super-rich surcharge.
Corporate rates (2019): **22% existing / 15% new manufacturing** (+surcharge-cess); **Pillar-2 global minimum: 15%**.
**Income-tax Act 2025** replaces the 1961 Act from **1 April 2026** — simplification recode ('tax year' replacing AY/PY language).
New personal regime (FY26): **nil tax up to ₹12 lakh** (rebate) — the default regime.
**GST 2.0 (from 22 Sept 2025)**: main slabs collapsed to **5% & 18%, with 40% on demerit-luxury goods**.
GST's constitutional kit: **101st Amendment; Arts 246A, 269A, 279A**; petroleum & alcohol outside (alcohol constitutionally).
**Professions tax ceiling ₹2,500/yr — Art 276** (needs amendment to raise).
Direct taxes ≈ **55-57% of gross central taxes** — the progressivity-share marker; **crypto: flat 30% + 1% TDS (2022)**.
